items.title: Championship momentum meets uncertainty in MLB
items.summary: SBJ looks at how the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays plan to cash in on their World Series runs while a lockout is expected when MLB's collective bargaining agreement expires on 1 December. The piece sets out what a title usually does for the following year: Toronto drew more than 3.3 million fans in 2026 after reaching the World Series, and the Dodgers grew sponsorship revenue 14.5% year on year according to SponsorUnited. It also recalls how the 2019 champion Nationals lost that momentum when COVID cut the season to 60 games, using ticket credits to limit refunds but still laying off business staff.
items.what_it_means: A championship creates a one-season window of demand for tickets, sponsorship and premium seats, and a labour stoppage could close that window before clubs convert it.

items.title: LIV Golf's impact felt across wider golf world
items.summary: As LIV Golf winds down, SBJ argues its lasting legacy is the change it forced across golf rather than the league itself. PGA Tour average purses rose from about $9.1M in 2021-22 to around $12.5M in 2026, and title sponsorships that could be bought for at most about $15M a year before LIV now run $30M to $35M a year for the top Championship Series events. The piece also credits LIV's broadcasts with pushing innovations such as live drone shot tracing and augmented reality graphics that are now common on PGA Tour telecasts.
items.what_it_means: A rival league that failed on its own still reset the price of sponsoring the incumbent, so brands are now paying roughly double for the same title rights.

items.title: Enhanced Games owner to acquire 77% of European promoter DEAG in all-stock deal valuing it at $115M
items.summary: Enhanced Group, the NYSE-listed owner of the Enhanced Games, has agreed to buy about 77% of Berlin-based live entertainment and ticketing company DEAG in an all-stock deal valuing DEAG at roughly US$115 million. DEAG stages more than 6,000 events a year, sells tickets through myticket.de and gigantic.com, and owns festivals and UK businesses including Kilimanjaro Live and Belladrum. Enhanced, which also sells telehealth and supplements, reported a second-quarter net loss of $61.9 million on $17.7 million revenue, and its market value is smaller than the deal value.
items.what_it_means: A loss-making sports and wellness start-up is buying an established promoter with ticketing and festivals, betting that live events give it the audience and revenue base it lacks.

items.title: Forum: Horse racing's trifecta of power, tension and objection
items.summary: Writing after the Breeders' Cup at Keeneland, SBJ's Abraham Madkour says US horse racing is consumed by tension between its power brokers over the future of the Triple Crown. He notes fans mostly know two things about the sport, the Kentucky Derby and the Triple Crown, and that the Derby's roughly 20 million viewers are what the other races market off. In June Churchill Downs offered $85 million for the Preakness Stakes rights, but Maryland, uneasy that the race could move to a Churchill-owned track in Virginia, matched and kept them.
items.what_it_means: When a sport's fan interest rests on one tentpole and one series, control of those events becomes the whole commercial fight.

items.title: NWSL prepping to move playoff games over schedule conflicts
items.summary: Citing ESPN and Bloomberg, SBJ reports that Shield winner Gotham FC could have to host a potential NWSL semifinal at the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium because its usual 25,000-seat home is booked for a New York Red Bulls friendly. San Diego Wave's home venue is also unavailable that night because of a college football game, and the national TV windows on 14 and 15 November are extremely unlikely to change. The league says it has been working with clubs and broadcasters on alternative sites, and the WNBA faced a similar problem during its finals.
items.what_it_means: Women's leagues that do not control their venues can see peak moments squeezed into smaller grounds, capping the crowds and revenue those moments should deliver.

items.title: Report: SNY cancels pair of shows, has layoffs
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that SNY, the regional sports network home of the Mets, has cancelled Baseball Night in New York and Sportsnite and laid off much of its editorial staff, effective immediately. It will keep producing Mets and Jets pre and postgame shows and the Mets Hot Stove Show. An SNY spokesperson said its site is pivoting from content to a promotional platform.
items.what_it_means: Regional sports networks are cutting back to live games and team shows, leaving the daily conversation around teams to other outlets.

items.title: Arctos' Ian Charles labels PE in college sports 'worst idea'
items.summary: Citing D Magazine, SBJ reports that Arctos Partners managing partner Ian Charles called private equity involvement in college sports the worst idea he has heard in his career, saying it seeks returns of at least 15 to 17 percent rather than acting as a safety net. He spoke alongside Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark and SMU athletic director Damon Evans, who said SMU has talked with three or four private equity groups but warned against rushing in without understanding the goal.
items.what_it_means: One of sport's biggest investors is warning that outside capital in college athletics comes with return demands that may not fit schools and their communities.
